---
title: Events and webhooks
description: How an app learns what changed in an instance, by following the event stream or receiving webhooks, and how the owner hears what needs attention.
job: A builder learns how an app hears about changes, by the event log, the stream and webhooks.
kind: concept
---

Marfa records each change to an item or edge as an **event** in one ordered log. An event is not a `core.event` item, which holds a calendar event. An app pulls events from the **event stream** when it needs every change, including what it missed while away, or has Marfa push them as **webhooks** when a service just reacts.

<EventFlow />

## The event log

Each event has an **event type**, such as `item.created`, `edge.deleted` or `rows.changed`, and an item event carries the item as it stands after the change. Changes to items, tags, extensions, rows and edges add events. **Other writes add none,** such as a change to a type, a key or a setting. [Events](/catalog/events) in the Catalog lists them all.

Event IDs rise, so the last ID an app handled, its **cursor**, says exactly where it stopped. The log keeps events for 30 days by default. A credential sees only the events about what its [type map](/build/access#what-a-credential-reaches) lets it read.

## The event stream

The [event stream](/reference/api/event-stream/streamEvents) is a connection your app keeps open. The CLI follows it here while another app saves a note:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa events --type core.note
```

```text
-  stream_cursor  18
-  stream_live  18
19  item.created  01a1fc3e-8e45-7226-8bb7-63467062037f
```

</Terminal>

The stream opens with `stream_cursor`, where the log stood then, replays each event your credential may see after the cursor you send in `Last-Event-ID`, marks the catch-up with `stream_live`, then sends each new event. Resume from your cursor and you get each later event **exactly once,** so save the cursor with what you applied. If the event after your cursor has aged out of the log, the stream ends with `catchup_too_old` and the app reads its data again ([Keep a copy in sync](/build/keep-in-sync)). A [working copy](/build/working-copies) follows the stream for you.

## Webhooks

A webhook works the other way round: Marfa posts each new event to a URL you register, for the event types you choose, with a credential that holds `webhooks.manage`. **Each delivery is signed** in `X-Marfa-Signature`, so your service can check it came from your instance. A failed attempt is tried again for hours; a redirect or a `4xx` other than `408` or `429` ends it.

**A webhook has no cursor and no replay:** it delivers only events written after you registered it, and they can arrive **out of order**, so a receiver orders by `event_id`, treats a repeated one as one delivery, and reads the item again when an exact state matters. A bulk write reaches webhooks only with `enable_fanout: true`. [Receive webhooks](/build/receive-webhooks) shows how to register one and check a delivery.

## When the owner needs to act

Marfa sends `attention.raised` when something new needs the owner's attention, such as a failed backup. **It reaches only a stream with no `type` filter, or a webhook subscribed to it, whose credential or maker holds `instance.read`;** a webhook's `type_filter` doesn't apply to it. It holds the entry's kind and a fixed description and **never its detail,** because a webhook posts outside the instance: `marfa attention` gives that.

The rules behind this page are in the [events](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md) and [reach](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/reach.md) chapters of the contract.
